solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Neurotic ignoring cold snaps as usual

indicators.note: to snap is to break, so the remaining letters of the word neurotic are broken up and rearranged
ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for cold is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: C is the usual abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An anxious person loses their temper in the cold, as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring cold' takes C out of NEUROTIC, leaving NEUROTI; 'snaps' then rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as usual is habitual, ordinary and done by regular custom, which is the adjectival sense here.

clue.text: Frightful Tory here? But so is a poet

indicators.note: frightful suggests something terribly mangled, so these thirteen letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A horrified question: is a ghastly Conservative here? Yes, and a bard too.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TORY HERE BUT SO rearrange into the poet's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Southey was an English Romantic, one of the Lake Poets and Poet Laureate from 1813.

clue.text: Sort out middle section of tune with composer

indicators.note: only the central letters are kept, so the outer letters of tune are dropped

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, of Boléro fame

explanation.surface: Fix the central passage of a melody along with its writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle a knot or a mystery is to work it out and resolve it.

clue.text: Private meal with no starter

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so here the first letter of the meal's word is removed

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: An intimate dinner that skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' plays on the first course of a meal; it means the first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Private thoughts are internal ones, hidden within and kept from others.

clue.text: Rogue may tease a mug

indicators.note: rogue describes something gone astray from its normal state, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoundrel might poke fun at a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' reads as a villain but is an adjective signalling that MAY TEASE be rearranged; 'mug' is British slang for a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug in British slang is a dupe, an easy target to be fleeced.

clue.text: Empty carriage destined to take away a joiner

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its shell, so just the first and last letters of carriage are used
taking away removes something, so the letter A is removed from the synonym for destined

parts.note: destined means meant, as in 'it was meant to be'

explanation.surface: A vacant coach is fated to lose a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty carriage' leaves CE; MEANT with its A taken away is MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortar or glue binds things together, so a bonding substance is something that joins parts.

clue.text: Man with no end in sight, repeating certain steps

indicators.note: the shortened word is said twice, so the same letters appear two times in a row
with no end means the final letter of the man's word is cut off

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow with no finish in view keeps doing the same dance moves.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP loses its end to give CHA, which is then doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin American ballroom dance is a set routine of particular dance moves.

clue.text: Religion in Wiltshire regularly occupying various imams

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit within, so the picked letters go inside the rearranged imams
various means in different forms, so the letters of imams are rearranged
regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of Wiltshire

explanation.surface: A faith is practised in Wiltshire at regular intervals by several Muslim clerics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' makes MAISM; 'regularly' takes the even letters; 'occupying' sets them after its first M. 'imams' tempts towards Islam, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a mystery cult popular among Roman soldiers, worshipping an Indo-Iranian god of light.

clue.text: Place under collar for punch

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece placed under comes after

parts.note: to nail and to collar both mean to catch or arrest
to set is to place

explanation.surface: Put something beneath a shirt neck to hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a blow but is the tool for driving nail heads below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a metal tool used, like a hole punch, to drive nail heads into wood.

clue.text: Creatures overcoming resistance with each lot of cold water

indicators.note: read as coming over and around, so one piece wraps around the letter for resistance

parts.note: creatures are living beings
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: Animals triumph over opposition, each group in icy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' puts R after the first two letters of the creatures' word; 'lot of cold water' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a northern arm of the Pacific between Alaska and Siberia, a large expanse of frigid ocean.

clue.text: Kindling catches on

definitions.meaning: small dry sticks used to start a fire
understands, realises, as in British slang 'he finally got it'

explanation.surface: Firewood that begins to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks serve as fire-starting material, and the informal verb meaning to grasp or realise is spelt identically.

clue.text: Tell all lighter Greeks to conserve energy

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe within, so the Greeks' word holds the letter for energy

parts.note: Thebans were the people of Thebes in ancient Greece
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Some sparky Greeks should conserve their power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' is not 'less heavy' but a SPILL, a taper for lighting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to reveal secrets or confess everything.

clue.text: Uninhibited person, say, on end of pier

indicators.note: in a charade, one piece placed on another comes after it
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of pier is used

parts.note: to say is to aver, to state firmly

explanation.surface: A wild partygoer is talking at the far end of a seaside pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A party animal who dances wildly is a free-spirited, unrestrained person.

clue.text: Thankless spy and head of security greeting teacher

indicators.note: read as 'without thanks': the British informal word for thanks is removed from the spy's name

parts.note: Mata Hari was a famous First World War spy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the first letter of security is used

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: An ungrateful agent and the security chief say hello to a schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thankless' means without TA (British for thanks): MATA HARI loses TA to give MAHARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu sage who gives spiritual guidance is a religious instructor or guru.

clue.text: Representative from state capital holding small article

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, so the capital's name wraps around the letter for small

parts.note: Salem is the capital of the US state of Oregon
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A delegate from an American state capital carries a minor item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state capital' means a US state's capital, Oregon's, not a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales rep is a travelling seller acting on behalf of a firm.

clue.text: Adriatic port targets problem with locks

parts.note: Split is a port in Croatia on the Adriatic Sea
ends are aims or targets, as in 'the end justifies the means'

explanation.surface: A Croatian harbour has trouble with its canal gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests canal or door locks, but it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that is frayed at the tips is a common complaint about one's tresses.

clue.text: Beam left at home by Lawrence initially

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next piece follows directly

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', had the initials T, E and L

explanation.surface: A timber was left in the house by Lawrence at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' here means Lawrence's initials, TEL (T. E. Lawrence), not just his first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lintel is the horizontal support spanning a doorway or window, a type of structural timber or stone.

clue.text: Conveyed cases almost once a week

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the word for conveyed wraps around the next

parts.note: conveyed means sent
nigh means almost, nearly

explanation.surface: Delivered packaging nearly every seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as archaic: this is an old word for a week, from 'seven nights'.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic term means a period of seven days, formerly used as fortnight still is.

clue.text: Posh fur fit for purpose

parts.note: U means upper-class, from the 1950s 'U and non-U' classification of British speech
sable is a luxurious fur

explanation.surface: An upmarket fur coat that does its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable is able to be put to work, i.e. suitable for the job intended.

clue.text: Hard worker supporting architect

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: Robert Adam was a famous Scottish architect
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A sturdy labourer props up a building designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding and firm in resolve; also once the name of an unbreakable stone.

clue.text: Drink that's exceedingly short, say

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: exceedingly means very
to mouth is to say or utter words

explanation.surface: A tot that is extremely small, let us say.
explanation.walkthrough: VERY cut short gives VER; MOUTH is the verb, to speak words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, an aperitif or cocktail ingredient.

clue.text: Universal acclaim for lift

parts.note: U is the British film classification for universal viewing
acclaim means praise

explanation.surface: Everyone applauds a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to raise or elevate something.

clue.text: Fifty per cent of dumb animals making money

indicators.note: fifty per cent is half, so the first half of dumb is used

parts.note: cats are animals

explanation.surface: Half of the speechless creatures are earning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold coins once used across Europe, and are slang for cash.

clue.text: Painful sensation of deer crossing English stream

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so the deer's word straddles the letter for English

parts.note: a hart is a male deer
burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: A deer feels pain as it fords an English brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts E after the first letter of the deer's word; the stream word is Scots and northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a burning ache in the chest caused by acid indigestion.

clue.text: Get rid of brushwood

definitions.meaning: cancel or abandon, as in 'scrap that plan'

explanation.surface: Clear away undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cancel or scrap; as a noun it is land covered with stunted shrubs and bushes.

clue.text: Divine smell, for example

definitions.meaning: to divine is to perceive or detect intuitively
smell is one of the five faculties, like sight and touch

explanation.surface: A heavenly smell, for one.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to feel or perceive; as a noun, one of the bodily faculties like taste or smell.

clue.text: Long period beginning in November

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the first letter of November is used

explanation.surface: A lengthy span of time starting in November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the period, but it is the verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it.

clue.text: Spy about right in capital of Asian country

indicators.note: about means around, so the spy's word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: an agent is a spy

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, so only the first letter of Asian is used

explanation.surface: An intelligence officer is close to the right in an Asian nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into AGENT after its A, giving ARGENT. 'capital' tempts towards a city, but it means a first letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American nation.

clue.text: Arrest reversed during crisis at surgery

indicators.note: the letters are read from right to left, so the picked run is turned backwards
during means within, so the letters sit inside the words crisis at surgery

explanation.surface: A cardiac arrest goes into reverse during an emergency at the doctor's.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'crisis at surgery' backwards (YREGRUSTASISIRC) and the run S-T-A-S-I-S sits across 'crisis', 'at' and 'surgery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill or stopped flow, as an arrest of circulation.

clue.text: University plugging dissertations in ancient Greek

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the letter for University fills a gap in the next word

parts.note: theses are long academic dissertations

explanation.surface: A university is filling up its classics essays on ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the mythical Athenian hero who slew the Minotaur.
